prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_G:
SNP Manifesto 2017 – Stronger for Scotland (summary)

The SNP asks voters to elect MPs who will always put Scotland’s interests first—ending Tory austerity, defending public services and family budgets, and ensuring Scotland’s voice is heard on Brexit and beyond. The party advances a progressive, pro‑equality, pro‑EU, anti‑austerity vision with more powers for Scotland and the right to choose Scotland’s future.

Fiscal plan and fair tax
- End austerity with a responsible plan to balance the current budget by 2021/22, use borrowing only for investment, reduce debt from 2019/20, and free up nearly £120bn UK‑wide for public services.
- UK‑wide 50p Additional Rate from 2018/19; oppose VAT and NI rises; reverse married couple’s allowance changes; restore bank levy, tax bankers’ bonuses; no further Corporation Tax cuts.
- Improve tax collection and transparency; halt HMRC office closures.

Protecting public services
- NHS: increase Scotland’s health budget by £2bn this parliament; pass on consequentials; oppose privatisation in England; back NHS reinstatement; fair pay for staff and safe staffing.
- Education: expand free childcare to 30 hours; invest to close the attainment gap; no grammar schools; protect free university tuition; restore post‑study work visas.
- Infrastructure: major investment in roads, rail (including HS2 to Scotland), digital (100% superfast by 2021), housing (50,000 affordable homes), and energy efficiency.

Jobs, growth, fair work
- Support business by doubling the Employment Allowance and raising the Annual Investment Allowance to £1m.
- Industrial strategy that works for Scotland; support oil and gas, decommissioning, and CCS; protect Scotch and key food/drink with geographic indications.
- Raise Minimum Wage to the real Living Wage; ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; repeal the Trade Union Act; strengthen equal pay enforcement; close gender, race, disability pay gaps; fair public sector pay.

Social security, equality and family budgets
- Scrap the two‑child cap and Rape Clause; end sanctions regime and benefit freeze; uprate benefits by at least CPI; halt flawed Universal Credit rollout; abolish Bedroom Tax UK‑wide (and in Scotland with new powers).
- Protect the pensions Triple Lock; support WASPI women; oppose State Pension Age rises beyond 66.
- Devolve full social security and employment powers to build a dignified, respect‑based system.

Brexit, Scotland’s choice, and more powers
- Majority in Scotland voted Remain; SNP will demand Scotland’s place at the negotiating table and inclusion of Single Market membership in the UK remit—protecting up to 80,000 Scottish jobs.
- Defend EU‑derived rights and funding; uphold the Sewel Convention; protect EU citizens’ rights now; devolve immigration to meet Scotland’s needs, including restoring post‑study visas and capping detention at 28 days.
- At the end of Brexit, Scotland must have a choice on independence. A vote for the SNP reinforces the Scottish Parliament’s mandate to decide the timing.

Democracy and defence
- Replace first‑past‑the‑post with proportional representation; votes at 16/17; votes for EU residents; abolish the House of Lords.
- Scrap Trident and redirect billions to public services; invest in conventional defence; protect Scottish bases; halt arms sales to regimes violating humanitarian law.

Climate and rural Scotland
- Champion renewables (onshore/offshore wind, wave, tidal), storage, and CCS; reform punitive grid transmission charges; oppose costly Hinkley C; match Scotland’s world‑leading climate ambition.
- End the UK’s “great rural robbery”: return £190m convergence uplift to Scottish farmers; repatriate all agriculture, fisheries and environment powers and funding; protect fishing communities and Single Market access.
- Improve rural broadband/mobile, fair delivery charges, and island connectivity.

International development and human rights
- Maintain 0.7% aid; embed climate justice and women’s rights; ethical trade; special envoy for global LGBTI rights; reinstate the Dubs scheme and create a humane, effective asylum system.

Core record in Scotland: free prescriptions; no Bedroom Tax; free personal care; expanded free childcare; free university tuition; record NHS investment and staffing; highest Living Wage coverage; more police, less crime; lower council tax than England; highest housebuilding rate in the UK.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – For the many, not the few (summary)

Labour sets out a choice to end a “rigged” status quo by rebuilding a fair economy and strong public services through investment, public accountability and rights at work.

Economy, tax and investment
- Upgrade the economy with a £250bn National Transformation Fund over 10 years and a National Investment Bank leveraging £250bn of lending, focused on all regions and small businesses.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate the day‑to‑day deficit within five years while borrowing to invest; debt lower by the end of the Parliament.
- Fair tax: no rises in income tax for 95% (those under £80k), no rises in VAT or personal NICs; top 5% and large corporations pay a bit more; clamp down on avoidance; protect and simplify for small firms.

Industrial strategy and ownership
- Mission-led strategy: 60% of energy from zero/renewable by 2030; 3% of GDP on R&D by 2030; skills, infrastructure and procurement reshaped to drive high-wage, high-skill jobs.
- Widen democratic ownership: double the co‑operative sector; “right to own” for employees; insource public services.
- Bring rail, water and Royal Mail into public ownership as contracts allow; regain control of energy networks and build a decentralised, publicly owned energy system.

Energy and climate
- Immediate household energy price cap while reforming the market.
- Insulate 4m homes; interest‑free loans for homeowners; stronger standards for renters.
- Ban fracking; back renewables and tidal lagoons; support nuclear within climate goals.
- New Clean Air Act; protect habitats; ban neonicotinoids; plant 1m native trees.

Brexit, trade and immigration
- Jobs‑first Brexit prioritising Single Market and Customs Union benefits; reject “no deal”; meaningful vote in Parliament.
- Guarantee EU nationals’ rights and reciprocal UK rights; no hard Irish border.
- Pro‑trade with high standards, transparency and SME support; human rights at the core.
- Fair migration rules ending scapegoating; crack down on exploitation; restore Migrant Impact Fund; welcome international students.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle‑to‑grave, free at point of use in FE; abolish university tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.
- Expand funded early years, extend 30 free hours to two‑year‑olds, strengthen Sure Start.
- Reverse school cuts; cap infant class sizes at under 30; free primary meals; end teacher pay cap; reduce high‑stakes testing.

Work, rights and incomes
- 20‑point plan: ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; abolish tribunal fees; Living Wage £10 by 2020; end public sector pay cap; 20:1 pay ratio on public contracts; strengthen equality and union rights; tackle bogus self‑employment.

Social security and pensions
- Keep the triple lock; protect universal pensioner benefits; fair transitional support for WASPI women.
- Scrap sanctions, Bedroom Tax, and punitive cuts; redesign Universal Credit; strengthen disability support under the UNCRPD; humane, holistic assessments.

Homes
- Build over 1m homes; at least 100k council/HA homes a year by end of Parliament.
- Private renters: three‑year tenancies, inflation‑linked rent caps, ban letting fees, minimum standards.
- Suspend Right to Buy where homes aren’t replaced; end rough sleeping with 4,000 homes and prevention.

NHS and care
- Over £30bn extra for the NHS; end pay cap; restore bursaries; reverse privatisation; guarantee 18‑week treatment and 4‑hour A&E targets; free hospital parking.
- Ring‑fence mental health; end out‑of‑area placements; school counselling.
- Build a National Care Service: £8bn this Parliament plus a long‑term funding settlement; real Living Wage for carers; end 15‑minute visits; cap lifetime care costs.

Safer, cleaner, connected communities
- 10,000 more police; 3,000 firefighters; 500 border guards; tackle violence against women and girls; rebuild youth services and local assets.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership; cap fares; expand bus franchising/municipal buses; complete HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail/Crossrail 2; nationwide electrification; boost cycling/walking; clean vehicles.

Democracy and equality
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; reform Lords; extend FOI; repeal Lobbying Act.
- Strengthen EHRC; gender audit of policy; 50% women cabinet; advance LGBT, BAME and disability rights (including UNCRPD into law).

Global Britain
- Foreign policy rooted in peace, human rights and international law; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales for use in Yemen pending UN investigation; climate leadership.
- Defence: spend at least 2% of GDP; renew Trident; strategic review; support UN peacekeeping; invest in UK defence industry and Armed Forces’ pay and housing.
- Development: keep 0.7% aid; tackle tax havens; support universal health coverage.

A programme to rebuild a fairer Britain that works for the many, not the few.
